title: Successful sign-in from a legacy client category
description: Detects successful Microsoft Entra sign-ins reported through selected legacy client categories. This is a policy-hygiene signal; the client label alone does not establish the authentication mechanism, bypass or compromise.

hypothesis.summary: An adversary may use a legacy authentication path to obtain access without modern authentication protections.
hypothesis.rationale: Legacy client categories can indicate authentication paths that do not support the same controls as modern clients, although approved compatibility exceptions can still exist.
hypothesis.detection_goal: Identify successful sign-ins from selected legacy client categories while leaving failed attempts and modern client categories unmatched.

triage.summary: Validate the client category, user, application, source network, authentication controls, and whether a documented compatibility exception exists.
steps: Confirm that the sign-in succeeded and determine which client or protocol produced the legacy category.
Review the user, application, source network, device context, and adjacent sign-in activity for anomalies.
Confirm whether the activity is covered by an approved exception and escalate unexplained access.
Treat this as change or policy monitoring; correlate with actor risk and an approved change record before opening an incident.
false_positives: Approved applications, devices, or migration exceptions that still use a reported legacy client category

validation.expected_outcome: Match a successful sign-in when ClientAppUsed is one of the selected legacy client categories; do not match failed sign-ins or modern client categories.

limitations: Authorized administration can produce this event. The rule does not independently establish compromise or completion of a command; assess identity, target and change approval.
Current-revision evidence is synthetic only. Validate full generated KQL, source fields, ingestion delay, alert volume and scoped exclusions in the target before enabling.
